Well, hello there. The dock doesn't get many visitors this early.
Hm. You have the look of someone who just arrived. Am I right?
Greetings. I'm Kuro. The cat, not the color, though both are true.
Ah, a new voice. That's a rare sound around here.
Hello, friend. I'd offer you a seat, but the barrel is taken by a gull.
Morning to you. The fish are shy today, but you seem braver.
Well met. I'm not much for words, but I'm much for company.
Ah, don't mind me. Old cats stare; it's our way of saying hello.
Good morning to you. The gulls are loud, but you seem quieter than them.
Ah, a new voice at the dock. The water doesn't mind, and neither do I.
Hello there. I was watching the tide. It watches back, you know.
Well now. You arrived without a splash. The good ones always do.
Morning, stranger. The fish aren't biting yet, but neither am I.
Hm. A face I don't know. That's a good excuse to sit and chat.
Greetings, traveler. My old bones say rain. Your bones will learn.
So you found my little spot. The cat on the barrel is friendly. Mostly.
Ah, don't stand on ceremony. The dock is for standing on, not for bowing.
Hello. The tide brought you in gentle. That's a good sign for the day.
Well met. I'm Kuro. I fish, I sit, I say things that sound wise.
Hmm. You look like a person with time on their hands. Good. I have some too.
A greeting to you. The harbor is calm. That means calm company is welcome.
Ah, a new face. The old cat blinks slow. That's hello in my language.
Greetings, friend of nobody yet. The sea makes friends slowly too.
Well now, a traveler. The road here is crooked, but you made it straight.
Hello there. I was mending nets. Now I'm mending the morning with talk.
You said hello without wanting anything. That's a rare catch, heh.
Morning to you. The fish are shy, but you don't seem shy at all.
Ah, another soul on the dock. The planks creak a welcome. Hear it?
Greetings. Old fishermen know everyone eventually. You're just early.
So. You've come to the quiet side. Good. Quiet suits a first hello.
Hello, stranger. My whiskers say you're alright. They're usually right.
Hm, a new voice. Voices are like lines: cast them slow and true.
Well met. I'd offer tea, but the kettle is out with the tide.
Ah, hello. I was counting waves. Lost count at three. You're a good distraction.
Greetings, traveler. No need for names yet. The harbor will learn yours.
You greet me first. That means you're polite, lost, or both. All fine.
Well now. No hurry in your step. That's rare as a two-headed minnow.
Morning, friend. The net is mended. The day is open. That's enough.
Ah, a greeting. That's like a first cast. You never know what bites, heh.
Greetings. A slow hello is worth ten fast ones. My grandmother said so.
Hello, traveler. Old cats nap, but we wake for kind voices. Yours is kind.
Well met, stranger. The dock remembers every boot. It likes yours.
Ah, don't mind the smell. That's the sea's perfume. You'll get used to it.
Hello, stranger. My boat is named Patience. She's got a twin: Waiting.
Greetings. The fog lifted just for you. Or maybe for me. Hard to say, heh.
Hello. The crates are for sitting, the sea is for looking. Pick both.
Hm. You said hello. The gulls said nothing. I trust you more already.
Morning, traveler. Sit if you like. The bench is old too; it won't judge.
Greetings, stranger. I'm not much for words, but I'm much for company.
Ah, hello. You greet an old cat like he's a person. I'll allow it, heh.
Hello there. I was watching the horizon. It was watching back, I think.
Well met. The morning catch was small, but the morning itself was big.
Morning to you. Any day above the water is a good one, I say.
Ah, a voice I don't know. That is a rare sort of morning, indeed.
Greetings, traveler. Mind the wet planks, they bite without teeth.
Hello, friend. I'd tip my hat, but the wind keeps it, heh.
Greetings. The harbor is calm, and calm harbors bring calm strangers.
Ah, you walk like someone with a question. Ask it slow; I'll listen slow.
Hello there. The fish are shy today, but you seem braver.
Morning, stranger. A cat greets with a blink, so consider this one.
